name: Scattered Spider
summary: Scattered Spider is a native English-speaking cybercriminal group active since at least 2022. The group initially targeted customer relationship management (CRM) providers, business process outsourcing (BPO) firms, and telecommunications and technology companies before expanding in 2023 to gaming, hospitality, retail, managed service provider (MSP), manufacturing, and financial sectors. Scattered Spider relies heavily on social engineering, including impersonating IT and help-desk staff, to gain initial access, bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA), and compromise enterprise networks. The group has adapted its tooling to evade endpoint detection and response (EDR) defenses and used ransomware for financial gain.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has used information from previous data breaches to identify employee names to be used in social engineering.
Scattered Spider has used a combination of credential phishing and social engineering to capture one-time-password (OTP) codes.
Scattered Spider has used domains mirroring corporate login portals to socially engineer victims into providing credentials.
Scattered Spider has used help desk voice-based phishing and also called employees at target organizations and compelled them to navigate to fake login portals using adversary-in-the-middle toolkits.
Scattered Spider has registered domains to spoof legitimate corporate login portals.
Scattered Spider has created matching fake social media profiles to support new accounts created in victim environments.
Scattered Spider has obtained malware to use at multiple stages of operations including information stealers, remote access tools, and ransomware.
Scattered Spider has obtained tools for use throughout the attack lifecycle to include remote access software, protocol tunneling and proxy tools, exploitation frameworks, and reconnaissance tools.
Scattered Spider has used compromised credentials for initial access.
Scattered Spider has used compromised Microsoft Entra ID accounts to pivot in victim environments.
Scattered Spider has leveraged legitimate remote management tools to maintain persistent access.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer has been distributed through cracked software downloads.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has been distributed as a malicious attachment within an email.
Scattered Spider has used the PowerShell cmdlet Get-ADUser.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can use `cmd.exe` to execute malicious code.
Scattered Spider has used the command shell to upload and install the Teleport remote access tool to a compromised vCenter Server Appliance.
Scattered Spider has impersonated organization IT and helpdesk staff to instruct victims to execute commercial remote access tools to gain initial access.
BlackCat: BlackCat can use `wmic.exe` to delete shadow copies on compromised networks.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can use a variety of API calls on a compromised host.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has relied on a victim to open a malicious attachment within an email for execution.
Scattered Spider has added accounts to the ESX Admins group to grant them full admin rights in vSphere.
Scattered Spider has assigned user access admin roles in order to gain Tenant Root Group management permissions in Azure.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can create `HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command` as a new registry key during privilege escalation.
Scattered Spider creates new user identities within the compromised organization.
Scattered Spider has run `SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH="/lib/systemd/ system/teleport.service` to establish persistence for the Teleport remote access tool.
After compromising user accounts, Scattered Spider registers their own MFA tokens.
Scattered Spider has added additional trusted locations to Azure AD conditional access policies.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can perform COM hijacking by setting the path to itself to the `HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command` key with a `DelegateExecute` parameter.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can add itself to the `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` and `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UIF2IS20VK` Registry keys.
Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.
Scattered Spider has deployed a malicious kernel driver through exploitation of CVE-2015-2291 in the Intel Ethernet diagnostics driver for Windows (iqvw64.sys).
Scattered Spider adds a federated identity provider to the victim’s SSO tenant and activates automatic account linking.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can use `sdclt.exe` to bypass UAC in Windows 10 to escalate privileges; for older Windows versions WarzoneRAT can use the IFileOperation exploit to bypass the UAC module.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has the ability to inject malicious DLLs into a specific process for privilege escalation.
BlackCat: BlackCat has the ability modify access tokens.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `MISC::AddSid` module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync beyond a single domain.
Scattered Spider has created volume shadow copies of virtual domain controller disks to extract the `NTDS.dit` file.
Scattered Spider has manually deleted emails notifying users of suspicious account activity.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can use XOR 0x45 to decrypt obfuscated code.
Scattered Spider creates inbound rules on the compromised email accounts of security personnel to automatically delete emails from vendor security products.

Scattered Spider utilized social engineering to compel IT help desk personnel to reset passwords and MFA tokens. Scattered Spider has also used Microsoft Teams to pose as internal IT support or help desk personnel.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can include a rootkit to hide processes, files, and startup.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer dynamically links key WinApi functions during execution.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer uses RC4 encryption for strings and command and control addresses to evade static detection.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer can remove files related to use and installation.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has been install via template injection through a malicious DLL embedded within a template RTF in a Word document.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can masquerade the Process Environment Block on a compromised host to hide its attempts to elevate privileges through `IFileOperation`.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has the ability of performing remote desktop access via a hVNC window for decreased visibility.
Scattered Spider has uninstalled and disabled security tools.
Scattered Spider has used self-signed and stolen certificates originally issued to NVIDIA and Global Software LLC.
Scattered Spider has created Amazon EC2 instances within the victim's environment.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCShadow` module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.

BlackCat: BlackCat can use Windows commands such as `fsutil behavior set SymLinkEvaluation R2L:1` to redirect file system access to a different location after gaining access into compromised networks.
BlackCat: BlackCat can clear Windows event logs using `wevtutil.exe`.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has the capability to grab passwords from numerous web browsers as well as from Outlook and Thunderbird email clients.
Scattered Spider retrieves browser cookies via Raccoon Stealer.
Scattered Spider Spider searches for credential storage documentation on a compromised host.
Scattered Spider enumerate and exfiltrate code-signing certificates from a compromised host.
LaZagne: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from memory to obtain account and password information.
Scattered Spider has extracted the `NTDS.dit` file by creating volume shadow copies of virtual domain controller disks.
LaZagne: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from LSA secrets to obtain account and password information.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credentials from databases, mail, and WiFi across multiple platforms.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credentials from Vault files.
Scattered Spider has searched for credentials in password vaults and Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions including HashiCorp Vault.
Scattered Spider has used multifactor authentication (MFA) fatigue by sending repeated MFA authentication requests to targets.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the SAM table.

procedures.text: LaZagne: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from MSCache to obtain account and password information.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from DCSync/NetSync.

procedures.text: LaZagne: LaZagne can use the `<PID>/maps` and `<PID>/mem` files to identify regex patterns to dump cleartext passwords from the browser's process memory.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credential information from /etc/shadow using the shadow.py module.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has the capability to install a live and offline keylogger, including through the use of the `GetAsyncKeyState` Windows API.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credentials from macOS Keychains.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create golden tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create silver tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO` module can create and export various types of authentication certificates.

Scattered Spider Spider enumerates a target organization for files and directories of interest, including source code, user provisioning, MFA device registration, network diagrams, and shared credentials in documents or spreadsheets.
Scattered Spider has executed scripts to identify the underlying operating system to ensure it uses the correct installation package for malicious payloads.
Scattered Spider can enumerate remote systems, such as VMware vCenter infrastructure.
Scattered Spider has enumerated Active Directory security groups including through the use of ADExplorer, ADRecon.ps1, and Get-ADUser.
Scattered Spider has enumerated legitimate domain accounts which are used in the targeted environment.
Scattered Spider has used network reconnaissance commands for discovery including `ping` and `nltest`.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer gathers information on the infected system owner and user.
Scattered Spider has enumerated the vSphere Admins and ESX Admins groups in targeted environments.
Scattered Spider has identified vSphere administrator accounts.
Scattered Spider retrieves browser histories via infostealer malware such as Raccoon Stealer.
Scattered Spider abused AWS Systems Manager Inventory to identify targets on the compromised network prior to lateral movement.

Scattered Spider enumerates cloud environments including Amazon Web Services (AWS) S3 buckets to identify server and backup management infrastructure, resource access, databases and storage containers.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer queries the Windows Registry to fingerprint the infected host via the `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid` key.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can obtain a list of processes on a compromised host.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer checks the privileges of running processes to determine if the running user is equivalent to `NT Authority\System`.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer gathers victim machine timezone information.
BlackCat: BlackCat has the ability to discover network shares on compromised networks.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer is capable of identifying running software on victim machines.

Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer collects the `Locale Name` of the infected device via `GetUserDefaultLocaleName` to determine whether the string `ru` is included, but in analyzed samples no action is taken if present.
BlackCat: BlackCat can enumerate local drives.
Scattered Spider has used RDP to enable lateral movement.
Scattered Spider has used SSH to move laterally in victim environments and to access the vSphere vCenter Server GUI.
Scattered Spider has also leveraged pre-existing AWS EC2 instances for lateral movement and data collection purposes.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT has the ability of performing remote desktop access via a VNC console.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `SEKURLSA::Pth` module can impersonate a user, with only a password hash, to execute arbitrary commands.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCSync` and `KERBEROS::PTT` modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
BlackCat: BlackCat can replicate itself across connected servers via `psexec`.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can collect data from a compromised host.
Scattered Spider stages data in a centralized database prior to exfiltration.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer can capture screenshots from victim systems.
Scattered Spider searched the victim’s Microsoft Exchange for emails about the intrusion and incident response.
Scattered Spider has redirected emails notifying users of suspicious account activity.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can access the webcam on a victim's machine.
Scattered Spider enumerates data stored within victim code repositories, such as internal GitHub repositories.
Scattered Spider threat actors search the victim’s Slack and Microsoft Teams for conversations about the intrusion and incident response.
Scattered Spider enumerates data stored in cloud resources for collection and exfiltration purposes.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer collects files and directories from victim systems based on configuration data downloaded from command and control servers.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer gathers information from repositories associated with cryptocurrency wallets and the Telegram messaging service.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer archives collected system information in a text f ile, `System info.txt`, prior to exfiltration.
Rclone: Rclone can compress files using `gzip` prior to exfiltration.
Scattered Spider has used proxy networks to hamper detection and has installed legitimate proxy tools on VMware vCenter and adversary-controlled VMs.
Scattered Spider has downloaded the Teleport remote access tool to compromised VMware vCenter Servers.

Scattered Spider has installed protocol-tunneling tools on VMware vCenter and adversary-controlled VMs, including Teleport.sh, Chisel (configured to communicate with trycloudflare[.]com subdomains), MobaXterm, ngrok, Pinggy, and Teleport.

In addition to directing victims to run remote software, Scattered Spider members themselves also deploy RMM software including TeamViewer, AnyDesk, LogMeIn, ngrok, and ConnectWise to establish persistence on the compromised network.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer uses HTTP, and particularly HTTP POST requests, for command and control actions.
Tor: Traffic traversing the Tor network will be forwarded to multiple nodes before exiting the Tor network and continuing on to its intended destination.

procedures.text: WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can communicate with its C2 server via TCP over port 5200.
ngrok: ngrok has been used by threat actors to proxy C2 connections to ngrok service subdomains.
ngrok: ngrok can provide DGA for C2 servers through the use of random URL strings that change every 12 hours.
WarzoneRAT: WarzoneRAT can encrypt its C2 with RC4 with the password `warzone160\x00`.
Tor: Tor encapsulates traffic in multiple layers of encryption, using TLS by default.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has exfiltrated data from compromised VMware vCenter servers through an established C2 channel using the Teleport remote access tool.
Scattered Spider has exfiltrated victim data to the MEGA file sharing site, SnowFlake, and AWS S3 buckets.
Raccoon Stealer: Raccoon Stealer will automatically collect and exfiltrate data identified in received configuration files from command and control nodes.
Rclone: The Rclone "chunker" overlay supports splitting large files in smaller chunks during upload to circumvent size limits.
Rclone: Rclone can exfiltrate data over SFTP or HTTPS via WebDAV.
Rclone: Rclone can exfiltrate data over FTP or HTTP, including HTTP via WebDAV.
ngrok: ngrok has been used by threat actors to configure servers for data exfiltration.
Scattered Spider has used BlackCat and DragonForce ransomware to encrypt files including on VMWare ESXi servers.
Scattered Spider has stopped the Volume Shadow Copy service on compromised hosts.
Scattered Spider has deployed ransomware on compromised hosts and threatened to leak stolen data for financial gain.
BlackCat: BlackCat has the ability to stop VM services on compromised networks.
BlackCat: BlackCat can change the desktop wallpaper on compromised hosts.
BlackCat: BlackCat has the ability to wipe VM snapshots on compromised networks.
